title: Blocked outputs, retention and deliberate voiding

blocks.text: Completed results are retained when ordinary output storage is full. The machine can pause with a finished batch waiting, even when power and input look correct. Drain the destination before expecting another batch.
The Void Upgrade explicitly permits disposal of completed results that do not fit. It is not a performance upgrade or a required part of automation. Leave it out when lossless storage is important.

Configured capacity reductions preserve existing excess contents rather than deleting them immediately. A previously full buffer may therefore exceed a newly lowered capacity until energy or items are withdrawn.

rows: Open the target inventory and verify actual free space for the exact item/components.
Check output side mode and receiver insertion rules.
Remove or account for any Void Upgrade.
Drain the blockage and confirm processing resumes.
For save/restart testing, use a copy of the world and compare exact counts before and after.
